accordion.behavior: APG accordion pattern (trigger is a button inside a heading, aria-expanded + aria-controls; Enter/Space toggle; Tab moves through triggers — arrow-key trigger navigation is optional per APG)

alert-dialog.behavior: APG alertdialog pattern (modal; role=alertdialog + aria-modal=true; focus trapped in the panel and Tab cycles; initial focus on the least destructive action; Esc closes and returns focus to the trigger; labelled by title, described by description — the description is REQUIRED, unlike dialog)

alert.behavior: APG alert pattern (in-flow, persistent message; role=alert for warning/critical, role=status for info/success; announced without moving focus; never auto-dismissed; any dismiss control is keyboard reachable)

aspect-ratio.behavior: None — layout primitive; no APG pattern (presentational wrapper, never focusable, adds no role; the hosted content keeps its own semantics)

avatar.behavior: Presentational identity image; no APG pattern (img semantics with alt text, or aria-hidden when adjacent text already names the person)

badge.behavior: Non-interactive status label; no APG pattern (presentational text — count-only badges require an accessible text alternative on the host)

breadcrumb.behavior: APG breadcrumb pattern (nav landmark with an accessible name; an ordered list of links; the last/current entry carries aria-current=page and is not a link; separators are decorative and hidden from assistive tech)

button-group.behavior: Grouping container — role=group with an accessible name; each child keeps its own button semantics and its own tab stop. A roving-tabindex toolbar (APG toolbar) is a different pattern and a different component; grouping never changes the children's keyboard model.

button.behavior: APG button pattern (Enter/Space activate; button role implicit)

calendar.behavior: APG grid pattern as used by the Date Picker Dialog: the month is a role=grid of week rows and day gridcells, with a roving tabindex so exactly one day is tabbable. Arrow keys move by day and by week, Home/End go to the start/end of the week, PageUp/PageDown change month (Shift+PageUp/PageDown change year), Enter/Space selects. Selected days carry aria-selected, unavailable days aria-disabled, and every day button's accessible name is its full date. The month/year caption names the grid and month changes are announced.

card.behavior: Static grouping container; no APG pattern (generic group semantics — interactive/selectable cards are a separate component, cf. Salt InteractableCard)

carousel.behavior: APG carousel pattern: the root is a region with aria-roledescription='carousel' and an accessible name; each slide is role=group with aria-roledescription='slide' and an 'N of M' label. Previous/next are real buttons, disabled (and aria-disabled) at the ends. With the region focused, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight move one slide (ArrowUp/ArrowDown when vertical). Slide changes are announced through a polite live region. Auto-rotation, when present, pauses on hover and on focus and always offers an explicit pause control.

chart.behavior: None — the plot itself is a graphic. Accessibility comes from a text alternative, not from the drawing: the root is role=img with an accessible name and description, and the same data is exposed as a visually-hidden table so keyboard and screen-reader users get the values. Interactive tooltips follow the APG tooltip pattern (shown on hover AND on focus, dismissible with Esc, never trapping the pointer); legend entries that toggle series are toggle buttons with aria-pressed. Series are distinguished by more than hue — pattern, marker shape or direct labels — so the chart survives colour-vision differences and monochrome print.

checkbox.behavior: APG checkbox pattern (Space toggles; mixed state via aria-checked=mixed)

collapsible.behavior: APG disclosure pattern (trigger is a button carrying aria-expanded + aria-controls; Enter/Space toggle; the panel is hidden from the accessibility tree while collapsed; focus never moves on toggle)

command.behavior: APG combobox pattern with a listbox popup, hosted in an APG dialog (modal) when used as a command palette. The input keeps DOM focus and is role=combobox with aria-expanded, aria-controls and aria-activedescendant; the results are role=listbox with role=option rows — options are never focused, only made active. ArrowDown/ArrowUp move the active option (wrapping at the ends), Home/End jump, Enter runs the active option, Esc dismisses the dialog and returns focus to the trigger. Filtering is live and the result count (including 'no results') is announced through a polite live region.

context-menu.behavior: APG menu pattern invoked by context action (pointer contextmenu, Shift+F10, or the ContextMenu key on the focused target; the panel opens at the invocation point with focus moved to it; arrow keys rove focus; Home/End jump; typeahead; Esc closes and returns focus to the target; role=menu / role=menuitem)

dialog.behavior: APG dialog (modal) pattern (focus trapped in panel; Tab cycles; Esc closes; focus returns to trigger on close; aria-modal=true; labelled by title, described by description)

drawer.behavior: APG dialog (modal) pattern, edge-anchored (focus trapped in panel; Esc closes; focus returns to trigger; aria-modal=true; bottom-edge drawers may add drag-to-dismiss — pointer enhancement only, keyboard dismissal stays Esc)

dropdown-menu.behavior: APG menu button pattern (trigger has aria-haspopup=menu + aria-expanded; Enter/Space/Down opens and focuses first item; arrow keys rove focus; typeahead; Esc closes and returns focus to trigger; role=menu / role=menuitem)

empty.behavior: None — presentational empty-state container; no APG pattern. The title is a real heading so the region is reachable by heading navigation, and any recovery affordance keeps its own button/link semantics. When the emptiness is the result of a completed load, the host region announces it (aria-live), not this container.

field.behavior: None — composition wrapper; native labeling semantics (label for/id, description and error wired via aria-describedby; error announced via aria-live or role=alert)

form.behavior: None — native <form> semantics. APG form/validation guidance: every control has an accessible name from its label (for/id), description and error are wired through aria-describedby, an invalid control carries aria-invalid, and the error text is announced (role=alert). Submission never relies on colour alone to signal failure; focus moves to the first invalid control.

hover-card.behavior: APG tooltip pattern widened to a non-modal preview disclosure (opens on pointer hover AND on keyboard focus of the trigger after an open delay, closes after a close delay on leave/blur; Esc dismisses without moving focus; focus is never pulled into the card; the trigger references it via aria-describedby; unlike a tooltip the card MAY hold rich content, and any interactive content inside it must also be reachable by Tab from the trigger — content that is only reachable by hovering is a contract violation)

icon.behavior: presentational (aria-hidden) unless labelled — no APG interaction pattern

input-group.behavior: None — role=group wrapping one native control plus adornments. The group is never focusable: focus lands on the hosted control and the group reflects it (:focus-within). Clicking an adornment that is not itself interactive forwards focus to the control. Interactive adornments (buttons) are real buttons inside the group and stay in the tab order after the control.

input-otp.behavior: Native text-input semantics on a single visually segmented field. ONE control owns the value, the focus and the tab stop (inputMode=numeric, autoComplete=one-time-code, maxLength=length); the cells are presentational (aria-hidden) and mirror the control's characters, with the caret drawn on the active cell. ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End/Backspace therefore behave natively, paste fills every cell at once, and screen readers announce one field — never N fields. Labelling and error wiring come from the field composition.

input.behavior: None — native <input> semantics (no APG pattern; labeling/description via field composition)

item.behavior: None of its own — a content-row primitive. Inside a group the wrapper takes role=list and each item role=listitem; an interactive item adopts the semantics of the element it renders as (link or button) and is then a single tab stop with its own focus ring. It never invents roving focus — a selectable collection is listbox/tree, a different pattern.

kbd.behavior: None — presentational. Renders the native <kbd> element so assistive tech announces the content as keyboard input; never focusable, never interactive, and pointer-inert so it cannot swallow clicks on the surface hosting it.

label.behavior: None — native <label> semantics (htmlFor/id association, or wrapping the control). Clicking or tapping transfers activation to the labelled control; the label itself is never a tab stop. It must not be replaced by a placeholder or an aria-label where a visible label is possible.

menubar.behavior: APG menubar pattern (role=menubar with a single tab stop for the whole bar; Left/Right rove between top-level triggers and wrap; Down opens the focused trigger's menu on its first item, Up on its last; while a menu is open, Left/Right close it and open the adjacent one; typeahead in both bar and menu; Esc closes the menu and returns focus to its trigger; role=menu / role=menuitem inside)

native-select.behavior: None beyond the platform's own — a native <select>. The user agent supplies the listbox behaviour (open, typeahead, arrow navigation, Esc), so no APG implementation is authored here; the component must not intercept those keys. Labelling and description come from field composition.

navigation-menu.behavior: APG disclosure-navigation pattern inside a nav landmark (links are links, never menuitems: role=navigation on the root, a plain list of items; a parent item's trigger is a button with aria-expanded + aria-controls on its panel; Left/Right when horizontal — Up/Down when vertical — move between top-level items, Home/End jump; Enter/Space toggle a panel, Down moves into the open panel, Esc closes it and returns focus to its trigger; Tab always leaves the menu; the current destination carries aria-current=page)

pagination.behavior: A navigation landmark: <nav> with an accessible name ('pagination') containing a list of page links. The current page carries aria-current='page' and is the only item so marked. Previous/next are real links/buttons that become aria-disabled at the ends rather than disappearing, so the control does not reflow. The ellipsis is decorative (aria-hidden) and is accompanied by a visually-hidden 'More pages' label. Every item is a normal tab stop — pagination uses no roving tabindex, because each destination is independently reachable.

popover.behavior: APG disclosure / non-modal dialog pattern (trigger has aria-haspopup=dialog + aria-expanded; focus moves into panel but is NOT trapped; Esc and outside click dismiss and return focus to trigger)

progress.behavior: APG meter/progressbar pattern (role=progressbar with aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax/aria-valuenow; omit aria-valuenow when indeterminate; label via aria-label/aria-labelledby)

radio-group.behavior: APG radio group pattern (roving tabindex; Arrow keys move selection; Space selects; one tab stop for the group)

rating.behavior: APG radio group pattern: one radio input per item sharing a group name; arrow keys move and select, Space selects the focused item; the group is labelled via aria-label/aria-labelledby and announces read-only via aria-readonly; each item announces its value ('<n> of <max>')

resizable.behavior: APG window splitter pattern: the handle is role=separator with aria-orientation, aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax/aria-valuenow (the primary panel's size as a percentage), aria-valuetext and aria-controls naming that panel. The handle is in the tab order. ArrowLeft/ArrowRight (ArrowUp/ArrowDown when the split is horizontal) move it by one step, Shift+Arrow by a larger step, Home/End move it to its limits, and Enter toggles between collapsed and the last size. Pointer dragging and keyboard must reach exactly the same positions.

scroll-area.behavior: None — a native scroll container with custom-drawn scrollbars. The viewport must stay keyboard-scrollable: it receives tabindex=0 (and a visible focus ring) whenever its content holds no focusable children, so keyboard-only users can reach it (WCAG 2.1.1), and it is labelled when it scrolls. The custom scrollbars are decorative (aria-hidden) and only replace the native ones visually — native scrolling, wheel, touch and scroll-anchoring behaviour are never intercepted, and the thumb is draggable with the pointer only.

select.behavior: APG combobox/listbox pattern (Alt+Down opens; typeahead; Esc dismisses; roving focus in listbox)

separator.behavior: APG separator pattern (decorative by default: hidden from assistive tech; semantic when it divides content regions: role=separator with aria-orientation; never focusable)

sheet.behavior: APG dialog (modal) pattern, edge-anchored (focus trapped in the panel; Tab cycles; Esc closes; focus returns to the opener on close; aria-modal=true; labelled by title, described by description). No pointer-drag dismissal — that is anatomy/drawer.json.

sidebar.behavior: A navigation landmark (<nav> with an accessible name) containing lists of links; the current destination carries aria-current='page'. The collapse control is a toggle button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, and collapsing hides the region from assistive tech only when it is truly hidden. Nested groups follow the APG disclosure pattern (button with aria-expanded controlling the sub-list); sub-lists are real nested lists so depth is announced. On narrow viewports the sidebar becomes an APG dialog (modal): focus is trapped, Esc dismisses, and focus returns to the trigger. Tab order follows visual order; the collapsed rail still exposes every item's name via its accessible name, never via tooltip alone.

skeleton.behavior: None — presentational placeholder. The placeholder itself is aria-hidden and the region it stands in for carries aria-busy=true, so assistive tech announces one loading status instead of reading a wall of empty shapes. It is never focusable and must not shift layout when the real content arrives.

slider.behavior: APG slider pattern: each thumb is role=slider with aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax/aria-valuenow (and aria-valuetext when the number is not self-explanatory), aria-orientation, and an accessible name. ArrowRight/ArrowUp increment and ArrowLeft/ArrowDown decrement by one step, PageUp/PageDown by a larger step, Home/End jump to min/max. Multi-thumb range sliders follow APG slider (multi-thumb): every thumb is its own role=slider, each separately tabbable, and thumbs may not cross.

sonner.behavior: APG alert/status host — the notification region, not the notification. An aria-live region (polite for tone info/success, assertive for warning/critical) that is never focusable and never moves focus; toasts are appended to it and announced in place; pointer hover or keyboard focus anywhere inside pauses every auto-dismiss timer in the region; each toast's own dismiss and action controls stay in the normal Tab order so a keyboard user can always reach them before the timer resumes.

spinner.behavior: APG progressbar pattern in its indeterminate form (role=progressbar with an accessible name and no aria-valuenow, wrapped in or paired with a polite live region so the busy state is announced; never focusable, never a tab stop; when a spinner stands in for a region's content that region carries aria-busy=true; the rotation is decorative — under prefers-reduced-motion it degrades to a static or fading indicator and the announcement carries the meaning)

stepper.behavior: Progress indicator, not an interactive composite (no APG widget pattern applies): ordered-list semantics (ol > li), aria-current="step" on the active step, per-step state (completed, error) conveyed as visually hidden text alongside the label; indicators and connectors are aria-hidden

switch.behavior: APG switch pattern (role=switch; Space/Enter toggle; aria-checked true/false)

table.behavior: Native table semantics (table / rowgroup / row / columnheader / cell; caption names the table). APG grid pattern applies only when cell navigation or row selection makes it interactive.

tabs.behavior: APG tabs pattern (tablist/tab/tabpanel; roving focus — arrow keys move between tabs, Home/End to first/last; activation is automatic on focus by default, manual via Enter/Space when panels are expensive — a declared behavior option, never a theme difference)

textarea.behavior: None — native <textarea> semantics (no APG pattern; labeling/description via field composition)

toast.behavior: APG alert pattern (role=alert for warning/critical, role=status for info/success; injected without moving focus; announced by assistive tech; hover pauses auto-dismiss; dismiss control keyboard reachable)

toggle-group.behavior: APG toolbar pattern over toggle buttons, with the role pair chosen by selection mode: single-select is role=radiogroup with role=radio items (aria-checked), multi-select is role=group with aria-pressed toggle buttons. Either way the group is ONE tab stop with a roving tabindex — ArrowRight/ArrowDown move to the next item, ArrowLeft/ArrowUp to the previous (wrapping), Home/End jump to the ends, and Enter/Space activates. In single-select mode arrowing moves selection with focus; in multi-select mode focus moves without toggling. Disabled items keep their place and stay reachable so the group's shape does not change.

toggle.behavior: APG button pattern with aria-pressed (Enter and Space toggle the pressed state; the accessible name stays the same in both states — the state is carried by aria-pressed, never by relabelling; the control is a single tab stop. A toggle placed in a group takes radio/checkbox semantics instead and roving focus — that is toggle-group, a different anatomy.)

tooltip.behavior: APG tooltip pattern (shows on trigger hover/focus after delay, hides on pointer leave/blur; Esc dismisses without moving focus; role=tooltip referenced by the trigger's aria-describedby; never contains interactive content)

tree.behavior: APG TreeView pattern: role=tree containing role=treeitem rows and role=group child lists; roving tabindex (one item tabbable); ArrowDown/ArrowUp move, ArrowRight expands then enters, ArrowLeft collapses then exits to parent, Home/End jump to first/last visible, Enter/Space select, typeahead moves to the next matching label; aria-level, aria-expanded and aria-selected on every item
